contemporary_baseline.title: Baseline training quality control
content: The corrected FP32 run completed all five folds without NaN/non-finite failure in the retained training logs. Fold 4, which had collapsed in the original AMP attempt, showed progressive learning and a final holdout ROC-AUC consistent with the other folds.
OOF completeness: 21,346 rows, 21,346 unique patient IDs, no duplicates, no missing probabilities.
Training QC decision: PASS for the corrected FP32 run.
The original AMP attempt remains explicitly archived as a failed-QC attempt because Fold 4 produced non-finite-gradient evidence and near-constant probabilities.

contemporary_baseline.title: Pretraining data overlap audit
content: Primary baseline: ConvNeXt V2 Tiny convnextv2_tiny.fcmae_ft_in1k. Public model documentation identifies ImageNet-1K as the upstream pretraining/fine-tuning dataset. No RSNA Pneumonia Challenge data are identified in that provenance.
This is a provenance classification, not proof that no visually related image exists anywhere in ImageNet. Stage-8 fine-tuning itself uses only canonical AURA development patients.

items: KERMANY_PROTOCOL = VERIFIED

Kermany image-level records expose a stable deidentified sample ID and path; age/sex/site metadata are not present in the canonical Stage-19 prediction table. The original cohort is pediatric; the revision must not infer individual demographic values not present in the artifacts.

sections.heading: Quantified shift
items: RSNA locked test: 5338 cases, 1203 pneumonia-positive, prevalence 22.5365%.
Kermany test: 624 cases, 390 pneumonia, prevalence 62.5000%.
Prevalence difference: 39.96 percentage points (Kermany higher).

At the unchanged threshold τ=0.47, A8 sensitivity changed from 0.8512 on RSNA to 0.7949 on Kermany, while specificity changed from 0.7715 to 0.9274. These are descriptive cross-cohort differences; the cohorts contain different individuals and no paired internal-vs-external test is used.
Class-conditional A8 score summaries are stored in 09_EXTERNAL_SCORE_DISTRIBUTION.csv. The score distributions differ across cohorts, but this does not identify a causal mechanism.

sections.heading: Known/observable domain differences
items: Population: Kermany is pediatric; the magnitude of the RSNA age-distribution shift cannot be quantified from the current analysis metadata.
Institution: Kermany originates from a different clinical source; RSNA site metadata are not used to claim a specific institutional effect.
File/image path: Kermany uses JPEG in the canonical external pipeline; RSNA uses DICOM. Canonical non-DICOM preprocessing was used without learned domain adaptation.
Prevalence: directly quantified above.
Label/case mix: Kermany is NORMAL-versus-PNEUMONIA pediatric classification; RSNA negatives are not equivalent to a strict healthy-normal control set.
No causal statement attributes performance changes specifically to age, acquisition, prevalence, institution, or case mix.

sections.heading: Selected branch upstream provenance
items: DenseNet121-XRV initialization: densenet121-res224-all. Current model-card provenance states training on nih-pc-chex-mimic_ch-google-openi-rsna.
EVA-X-S initialization: eva_x_small_patch16_merged520k_mim.pt. The EVA-X publication defines Merged520k as frontal images from ChestX-ray14, CheXpert and MIMIC-CXR.

sections.heading: Candidate implications
items: NIH ChestX-ray14: CONFIRMED upstream overlap in XRV and EVA-X.
CheXpert: CONFIRMED upstream overlap in XRV and EVA-X.
MIMIC-CXR: CONFIRMED upstream overlap in XRV and EVA-X.
PadChest: CONFIRMED upstream overlap in XRV; not listed in EVA-X Merged520k.
VinDr-CXR: NO KNOWN upstream overlap from the documented XRV-all and EVA-X provenance, but the public release removes PatientID, preventing strict patient-cluster verification.

Upstream exposure does not make these datasets invalid for every scientific use, but it weakens their status as clean independent external validation of this exact frozen system, especially when the exposure is supervised on related pathology labels.

transformer_xai.title: Hook non-interference and state-safety test
content: On the deterministic preflight case, probability before/after LayerCAM instrumentation was:

Repeated EVA LayerCAM generation passed the script's deterministic np.allclose check (rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-7). The complete run re-hashed the deployment checkpoints after attribution: both hashes were unchanged, and checkpoint_unchanged=true. The attribution script clears gradients after use and does not retrain or update parameters.

items: Status: VERIFIED_ROW_MAJOR.

Dynamic instrumentation of the exact frozen EVA-X-S deployment model captured the input to blocks.0 as [1, 197, 384]. The sequence contains 197 tokens with embedding dimension 384: one verified class/prefix token followed by 196 patch tokens. The model exposes num_prefix_tokens=1, cls_token shape [1, 1, 384], patch size 16×16, and grid 14×14. No additional prefix/register/distillation tokens were observed (other_prefix_tokens=0).

sections.heading: Structural patch perturbation test
items: patch (0,0) -> token 1 (expected 1): PASS
patch (0,1) -> token 2 (expected 2): PASS
patch (1,0) -> token 15 (expected 15): PASS
patch (13,13) -> token 196 (expected 196): PASS

The patch sequence is therefore row-major raster ordered after the leading class token. The historical rule that removes one leading token when N-1 is a perfect square yields the same retained 196 patch tokens for this exact checkpoint (historical_heuristic_equivalent=true). This establishes equivalence for the historical implementation; the revised specification should state the verified one-prefix-token structure directly rather than infer it from sequence length alone.
Analysis origin: POST_HOC_MULTIPLICITY_CORRECTION.

sections.heading: Family A — model vs localization baselines
items: Scientific question: Do the frozen Hybrid CNN–ViT LayerCAM maps exceed simple non-model localization priors across the four prespecified localization measures?
Included: 4 metrics × 4 baselines = 16 paired contrasts.
Population: 1,203 GT-positive locked RSNA cases.
Raw test: two-sided paired sign-flip randomization of the case-level mean difference, 20,000 Monte Carlo permutations with +1 correction.
Primary correction: Holm FWER, alpha=0.05.
Sensitivity: BH-FDR; Bonferroni familywise bootstrap interval sensitivity (99.6875% nominal per contrast).
Effect uncertainty: original unadjusted 95% paired-bootstrap CI, 2,000 resamples, seed 42 plus canonical metric offsets.

sections.heading: Family B — TP vs FN localization
items: Scientific question: Is localization systematically stronger for true-positive than false-negative locked-test cases?
Canonical inferential report contains five related metrics: Pointing Game, IoU, localization score, energy inside GT, and peak distance.

Family size: 5. Four are displayed in Fig. 6a; peak distance is retained because it appears in the canonical inferential output and is named among the Methods localization metrics. Excluding it would leave an orphan p-value.
Population: TP=1,024, FN=179; independent groups.
Raw test: two-sided Mann–Whitney U; effect size: Cliff's delta.
Primary correction: Holm FWER across all five canonical tests; BH-FDR sensitivity.

sections.heading: Family C — EVA attribution-method sensitivity
items: Scientific question: Are EVA localization findings sensitive to the attribution method?
Included: four prespecified EVA LayerCAM-vs-Integrated-Gradients localization metrics.
Family size: 4.
Primary correction: Holm FWER already applied in Stage 7. Stage 9 verifies, and does not double-adjust, those p-values.

sections.heading: Family C2 — IG TP-vs-FN supporting sensitivity
items: Scientific question: Does the TP-vs-FN pattern persist under EVA Integrated Gradients?
Included: four Stage-7 supporting Mann–Whitney tests.
Family size: 4.
Primary correction: Holm FWER in Stage 9; BH-FDR sensitivity.

sections.heading: Family D — perturbation faithfulness
items: Deletion drop and retention ratio are descriptive quantities with marginal bootstrap CIs. No formal null-hypothesis p-values were used; no multiplicity correction is required.

sections.heading: Family E — outside-lung analysis
items: Current manuscript/reports use descriptive means/sensitivity quantities rather than a family of formal hypothesis tests. No multiplicity correction is required. No causal inference is permitted.
Family definitions follow distinct scientific claims and were frozen for this revision-era audit before adjusted results were interpreted.

xai_statistics.title: Faithfulness multiplicity audit
content: The canonical faithfulness output contains two descriptive quantities on the same deterministic n=256 cohort:
deletion confidence drop: mean 0.215727, marginal 95% CI [0.202129, 0.228843];
retention probability ratio: mean 0.808899, marginal 95% CI [0.779430, 0.841685].

No formal null-hypothesis p-values are present in the canonical faithfulness artifact, and Stage 7 did not add a comparator-faithfulness test family. Therefore FAITHFULNESS_MULTIPLICITY = NOT_REQUIRED for the current manuscript. These CIs remain descriptive marginal intervals; they do not establish causal reasoning or complete A8 faithfulness.

xai_statistics.title: Outside-lung multiplicity audit
content: The provenance-verified regenerated-mask sensitivity file contains n=1203 cases. Mean outside-lung ratio is 0.215528 overall, 0.182310 for TP cases, and 0.405557 for FN cases.

The manuscript uses these values descriptively and explicitly avoids a causal statement. No canonical p-value family is attached to this regenerated-mask sensitivity analysis. Therefore OUTSIDE_LUNG_MULTIPLICITY = NOT_REQUIRED for the current claims. Any later formal TP-vs-FN outside-lung test would constitute a new inferential family and must be prespecified separately.
